c.tagline: Uganda's hilly, hospitable capital on the shores of Lake Victoria.

taxi.color: white with blue stripe (special-hire) / branded app cars
taxi.fareNote: Special-hire taxis and boda-bodas negotiate a fixed price upfront rather than using a meter; ride-hailing apps (Uber, Bolt) show a fixed fare in-app before you ride.

emergency.medical: 999 or 112 (public ambulance coverage is limited; private services such as St. John Ambulance +256 800 199 555 are commonly used)
emergency.note: Emergency response can be slow outside central areas; hotels can usually arrange faster private assistance.

avoid.reason: Pickpocketing around the taxi parks/Owino market; caution at night; boda-boda theft

hood_desc: Kampala's leafy, hilly diplomatic quarter of embassies and upscale homes, packed with boutique hotels, spas and fine dining; suits business travelers and those wanting a quiet, secure base close to downtown.
The historic commercial and government core with markets, banks and Kampala's best-known hotels within walking distance of Parliament; suits first-timers who want to be in the thick of downtown.

A green, affluent suburb of bungalows and serviced apartments popular with expats, anchored by Village Mall and quieter than the center; suits longer stays and travelers wanting calm with easy access in.
Kampala's round-the-clock nightlife and bar strip along Ggaba Road, full of cheap eats, clubs and backpacker hostels; suits younger travelers and anyone who wants to be near the action after dark.
Known as Tank Hill for its panoramic views over the city and Lake Victoria, a quieter upscale residential area with boutique lodges; suits travelers wanting scenery and a relaxed, leafy retreat.

water.note: Tap water isn't reliably safe even after treatment; use bottled or filtered water.

transit.pay: Matatus and city buses are paid in cash directly to the conductor/driver, with informal per-route fares; there is no citywide fare card. Ride-hailing apps (Uber, Bolt, SafeBoda) are paid via the app or cash to the driver.
transit.hours: Matatus and buses generally run about 6am-9pm; boda-bodas and app-based rides operate later into the night and are the safer option after dark.
transit.note: Kampala has no metro or tram system; most visitors rely on shared matatu minibuses, boda-boda motorcycle taxis, and ride-hailing apps, with a small commuter rail line serving outlying suburbs.

bus: Intercity coaches (Link, Trinity, YY) to regional towns
ferry: Lake Victoria ferry to the Ssese Islands (from Nakiwogo, near Entebbe)

airport.name: Entebbe International Airport (EBB)
airport.drive: 45-75 min depending on traffic; Entebbe Expressway toll road cuts the trip to around 45 min

transit.m: Boda-boda motorcycle taxi (not ideal with luggage)

tip.r: Tipping isn't mandatory but 5-10% at sit-down restaurants and small tips for tour guides, drivers and porters are appreciated and increasingly expected in tourist-facing venues.

food.name: Rolex
food.desc: Uganda's national street snack: a fresh chapati wrapped around a fried egg omelette with tomato, onion and cabbage, rolled hot to order.

places.name: Wandegeya rolex stalls
places.note: The student strip below Makerere; charcoal griddles run from dawn until very late, cheapest rolex in town.

places.name: Kikoni rolex stands
places.note: Makerere back-gate stands where the rolex was popularised; ask for a double-egg kikomando roll.

places.name: Cafe Javas
places.note: Homegrown cafe chain doing a tidy plated rolex with proper coffee if you want it sit-down.

food.name: Luwombo
food.desc: Royal Buganda dish of chicken, beef, goat or groundnut stew tied into smoked banana leaves and steamed, served with matoke and rice.

places.name: The Seasons Bistro
places.note: Serves chicken, beef, goat and groundnut luwombo daily; one of the most consistent versions in the city.

places.name: 2K Restaurant
places.note: Big local buffet famous for luwombo and pilau in generous portions at local prices.

places.name: Shaka Zulu Foods
places.note: Neighbourhood canteen doing groundnut, beef and mushroom luwombo alongside katogo.

food.name: Matoke with groundnut sauce
food.desc: Steamed green cooking banana mashed soft in banana leaves and drowned in binyebwa, a rich peanut sauce; the everyday Ugandan staple plate.

places.name: 2K Restaurant
places.note: Buffet line where you point at matoke, binyebwa, beans and greens and pay a few thousand shillings.

places.name: Nakasero Market food stalls
places.note: Market kitchens serve matoke and groundnut sauce to traders from mid-morning; busy means fresh.

places.name: Ekitoobero Market Kitchen
places.note: Local-food specialist built around market produce and traditional Ganda staples.

food.name: Muchomo
food.desc: Goat or beef skewers rubbed with salt and chilli and grilled over charcoal, served with kachumbari salad, gonja plantain and a squeeze of lemon.

places.name: Jeans Pub
places.note: Long-running nyama choma garden, packed with the East African grilled-meat crowd at weekends.

places.name: Kungo Maito
places.note: Cheap by-the-kilo goat grill near KIU hostels; a plate starts around 2,500 shillings.

places.name: The Lawns
places.note: Upscale garden grill known for game meat and well-executed nyama choma platters.

food.name: Katogo
food.desc: Kampala's breakfast one-pot: green banana simmered together with offal, beef or beans until it collapses into a thick savoury stew.

places.name: Shaka Zulu Foods
places.note: Does both katogo offal and katogo beef; a morning fixture for the Bugolobi office crowd.

places.name: Wandegeya food stalls
places.note: Cheap early-morning katogo pots ladled straight from the sufuria; sold out by mid-morning.

places.name: 2K Restaurant
places.note: Reliable breakfast katogo before the lunch buffet takes over the counters.

food.name: Grilled Lake Victoria tilapia
food.desc: Whole tilapia from the lake, scored and grilled or deep-fried, served with cassava, kachumbari and chilli; best eaten at a landing site.

places.name: Ggaba landing site fish grills
places.note: Buy the fish off the boat and have it grilled a few metres away; go early afternoon.

places.name: Munyonyo lakeside grills
places.note: Lakeshore stalls and terraces doing whole fried tilapia with a Lake Victoria view.

places.name: Little Ritz in Africa
places.note: Sit-down local kitchen that plates tilapia with matoke and greens for people who want a table.

food.name: Ugandan coffee
food.desc: Uganda grows both robusta and highland arabica, and Kampala's cafe scene roasts it locally; ask for a single-origin from Sipi Falls or Mount Elgon.

places.name: Endiro Coffee
places.note: Ugandan-owned social-enterprise roaster; traceable single-origin beans and good pour-overs.

places.name: 1000 Cups Coffee House
places.note: Kampala's original speciality coffee house, pouring Ugandan estate coffees since the 1990s.

places.name: Cafe Javas
places.note: Homegrown chain, open long hours, easiest place to try Ugandan beans with breakfast.

food.name: Uganda Waragi
food.desc: The country's own gin, distilled from cane spirit and juniper; drunk neat, with tonic, or in a passionfruit or ginger mix at almost every bar.

places.name: Bubbles O'Leary
places.note: Long-standing Irish pub with a garden; a dependable place to try waragi and tonic.

places.name: Cayenne Restaurant and Lounge
places.note: Poolside bar where waragi cocktails and passionfruit mixes are the local order.

places.name: Jeans Pub
places.note: Nyama choma garden where waragi and cold Bell Lager come with the grilled goat.

landmarks: Kasubi Tombs
This UNESCO World Heritage site of thatched-roof royal mausoleums honors four Buganda kings, showcasing remarkable traditional architecture within a sacred forested compound.
Uganda Martyrs Shrine, Namugongo
A striking copper-domed basilica built on the site where 22 Christian converts were executed in 1886, drawing pilgrims from across East Africa each June.
Bahá'í House of Worship
The only Bahá'í temple in Africa, this graceful domed structure sits amid lush hilltop gardens overlooking Kampala, welcoming visitors of all faiths.
Uganda National Mosque (Gaddafi Mosque)
East Africa's largest mosque, crowned by a soaring minaret with panoramic city views, blends Arabic and African architectural influences atop Old Kampala Hill.
Namirembe Cathedral
Perched on one of Kampala's iconic hills, this Anglican cathedral with its red-brick dome has anchored the city's skyline and Christian heritage since 1919.
Rubaga Cathedral
Also known as Lubaga Cathedral, this twin-towered Catholic cathedral crowns another of Kampala's seven hills, offering sweeping views over the city.
Uganda Museum
The country's oldest museum displays traditional musical instruments, royal artifacts, and archaeological finds tracing Uganda's ethnic and natural history.
Kabaka's Lake
A hand-dug 19th-century artificial lake commissioned by the Buganda king, now a tranquil spot for boating and birdwatching near the royal palace.
Bulange Mengo (Buganda Parliament)
The seat of the Buganda Kingdom's traditional parliament, this stately colonial-era building remains a symbol of Buganda's enduring cultural and political identity.
Independence Monument
A bronze statue of a mother unwrapping her swaddled child toward the sky, symbolizing Uganda's 1962 liberation from British colonial rule.

train.note: There are no international passenger trains from Kampala - the old metre-gauge line to Kenya carries freight only and the Standard Gauge Railway is still under construction. URC runs a limited city commuter passenger train between Kampala station and Mukono (via Namanve); check urc.go.ug for the current schedule.

bus.note: Cross-border coaches run east to Nairobi and Mombasa (Kenya) and south-west to Kigali (Rwanda), with onward links toward Dar es Salaam and Juba. Buses depart from the Kampala bus parks/Namayiba area; overnight departures are common, so carry your passport for the Malaba (Kenya) or Cyanika/Gatuna (Rwanda) borders.

ferry.note: There are no scheduled international passenger ferries. Uganda sits on Lake Victoria but the historic MV steamer services to Tanzania and Kenya no longer carry regular passengers; local motorboats serve the Ssese Islands from Entebbe/Nakiwogo.

half.name: Jinja (Source of the Nile)
half.blurb: Adventure hub where the White Nile begins, famed for white-water rafting and river cruises.

half.name: Mabamba Swamp
half.blurb: Vast papyrus wetland explored by dugout canoe, prized for spotting the rare shoebill stork.

half.name: Entebbe
half.blurb: Lakeside town with botanical gardens and a wildlife center along the shores of Lake Victoria.

half.name: Ngamba Island
half.blurb: Forested island sanctuary on Lake Victoria home to rescued and orphaned chimpanzees.

half.name: Mabira Forest
half.blurb: Lush rainforest reserve offering shaded nature trails, ziplining, and rich birdlife and primates.

full.name: Ziwa Rhino Sanctuary
full.blurb: The only place to track southern white rhinos on foot in the wild in Uganda.
